author: Jessica Patterson
title: Former Scioto County Commissioner, wife sentenced in theft in office case - NewsBreak
text:
By Jessica Patterson Lane Ball ,
13 hours ago
SCIOTO COUNTY, Ohio (WOWK) - A former Scioto County Commissioner and his wife have been sentenced for their roles in what the Ohio State Auditor has called a "public contracting scheme."
Bryan Davis appeared in court Wednesday, where he was sentenced to 30 months in prison for one count and an 11-month sentence for another, which will be served concurrently with the 30-month sentence.
After he is released from prison, Davis will be on probation for two years.
Davis is also required to pay Scioto County $67,808.67 in restitution and $512.50 to the State Auditor's Office. He must also forfeit his retirement account, pay the Scioto County Commission back the salary he has received and pay the court costs for the proceedings.
As part of his sentence, Davis is also banned from running for or serving in public office.
In court, Davis waived his right to appeal.
Lorinda Davis, who pleaded guilty to one felony count of tampering with evidence in the case, was sentenced to two years of community control or criminal probation. She has also been ordered to pay a supervisory fee and court proceedings costs.
The couple was indicted, along with Robert Horton and his wife, last year after an investigation by the Auditor’s Office’s Special Investigations Unit into an alleged scheme involving the Southern Ohio Port Authority, as well as the Southern Ohio Aeronautical Regional (SOAR) Business Park Portsmouth area, the Auditor says. According to Faber, Horton was head of the Southern Ohio Port Authority and the Scioto County Economic Development Department.
Faber says his office launched the investigation following a complaint about a “potential unlawful interest in a public contract” between the Port Authority and an out-of-state company for a building at the SOAR Business Park.
According to Faber’s Office, the charges against the Hortons are still pending in the Scioto County Common Pleas Court.
The indictments accuse Robert Horton of allegedly receiving kickbacks for securing the construction contract. Faber says the indictments accuse Davis of using his position on the Scioto County Commission to secure the public funding and the contract.
The Davises pleaded guilty to the charges in July.
Davis was suspended from the commission following his indictment and calls from his fellow commissioners to resign. Once his suspension was approved, the vacant seat was filled in November 2025 by Will Mault, who in May won the Republican Primary race for the seat . There is no Democratic challenger for the November race.
